transcript: I have not had a play confuse me as much as Staff Meal at Playwrights Horizons in awhile, and so I am dying to hear other people's takes on it. Mostly taking place at a restaurant, this play starts off somewhat straightforward but then completely transforms, introduces new characters, and scrambles up pretty much everything you thought you knew about the rules of the play and the world of it. I would describe this play as very quirky with some funny moments but there's a darkness and sense of meandering that feels very intentional. Also, there are characters that feel like they belong in completely different place from one another and the show just goes in so many different directions. I felt like I was projecting meaning onto the piece more than the piece was telling me its meaning. Overall though I found the piece very intriguing and I actually would love to see it again once it's no longer in previews. With that, another program for my collection.
